methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -c copy output.mkv.
methods.limits: Default stream selection picks one stream of each kind. Use explicit mapping when the whole track set matters.

methods.steps: Open Source, select the MP4, choose a Matroska preset such as H.264 MKV 1080p30, set the Save As destination and select Start.
methods.limits: The presets set their own encoders, so the video is encoded again; this suits a file whose codec also needs to change.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i input.mxf -c:v libx264 -c:a aac output.mp4.
methods.limits: Requires the source decoder and the libx264 and AAC encoders in the build; defaults do not copy every MXF stream.

methods.steps: Select Open Source and choose the MXF, pick a preset such as Fast 1080p30, set the destination under To, and select Start.
methods.limits: The preset sets the encoder and frame settings, so the video is encoded again.

methods.steps: Run magick input.psd output.pdf.
methods.limits: The formats page lists both PSD and PDF as readable and writable.

methods.steps: Open the PSD using File > Open, then choose File > Export As, pick PDF and save the export.
methods.limits: An exported document is distinct from the editable PSD.

methods.steps: Open the WebP and choose File > Export As. Edit the extension in the Name field to .ico, or pick ICO under Select File Type, then export; the ICO dialog sets the color depth and offers a Compressed (PNG) checkbox.
methods.limits: Not all programs support reading icons saved with the Compressed (PNG) option.

methods.steps: In Python, open the WebP with Image.open and call save with a .ico filename; pass sizes=[(16,16),(32,32),(48,48)] to put several icon sizes in one file.
methods.limits: Needs libwebp to read WebP; any size bigger than the original or 256 is ignored.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i input.webp output.ico.
methods.limits: FFmpeg's documentation lists WebP decoding and ICO reading and writing.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i input.aif -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 192k output.mp3.
methods.limits: Requires a build with the LAME encoder; the b option sets the bitrate for CBR or ABR.

methods.steps: Choose File > Import > Audio and select the AIF, then choose File > Export Audio and pick MP3 as the format.
methods.limits: The bit rate modes are Preset, Variable, Average and Constant, and Standard is the default preset; MP3 export always uses joint stereo.

methods.steps: Open the AVIF in GIMP 2.10.22 or later and choose File > Export As. Edit the extension in the Name field to .gif, or pick GIF under Select File Type, then export.
methods.limits: AVIF reading needs GIMP 2.10.22 or newer; GIMP only supports exporting a GIF with a maximum of 256 colors.

methods.steps: Run magick input.avif output.gif.
methods.limits: Check that your ImageMagick build has AVIF support; GIF output is limited to 256 palette entries.

methods.steps: In Python, open the AVIF with Image.open and call save with a .gif filename.
methods.limits: Pillow decodes AVIF as 8-bit only.

methods.steps: Run magick input.jpg output.bmp.
methods.limits: BMP is written as version 4 by default; the BMP3 and BMP2 tags give versions 3 and 2.

methods.steps: Open the JPG and choose File > Export As. Edit the extension in the Name field to .bmp, or pick BMP under Select File Type, then export and choose options in the BMP dialog.
methods.limits: The BMP dialog has a Write color space information checkbox (not all programs can read it) and an RGB format list.

methods.steps: In Python, open the JPG with Image.open and call save with a filename ending in .bmp.
methods.limits: Pillow reads and writes BMP; save takes the format from the extension when none is given.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i input.mkv -vf palettegen palette.png, then ffmpeg -i input.mkv -i palette.png -lavfi paletteuse output.gif.
methods.limits: The palettegen filter generates one palette for a whole video stream.

methods.steps: Put the MKV on the timeline, choose File > Render, select GIF High Quality under Generic, choose Full Project or Selected Zone, then select Render to File.
methods.limits: Selected Zone renders only the part of the project that has a zone selected.

methods.steps: Open the PNG and choose File > Export As. Edit the extension in the Name field to .cur, or pick it under Select File Type, then export; in the Windows Cursor dialog set the save type, the Compressed (PNG) option and Hot spot X and Hot spot Y.
methods.limits: Some programs can't read PNG-compressed entries; the dialog notes that not all programs support reading this type of icon.

methods.steps: Open the PNG, select the desired area, and choose Image > Create New Cursor from Selection. Choose cursor formats, then use Draw > Set Cursor Hot Spot to place the active point.
methods.limits: The hot spot change applies to all formats of the same size.

methods.steps: Load the PNG, set HotspotX and HotspotY on image.Frames.RootFrame.Metadata.GetCurMetadata(), and save to a .cur filename with new CurEncoder().
methods.limits: Hotspots should be chosen from the cursor design and not copied from another size.

methods.steps: Run magick -density 150 input.ai output.jpg.
methods.limits: -density sets the canvas resolution while rendering vector formats such as PostScript and PDF; ImageMagick lists AI (Adobe Illustrator CS2) as readable.

methods.steps: Run gs -dBATCH -dNOPAUSE -sDEVICE=jpeg -r150 -sOutputFile=page-%d.jpg input.ai.
methods.limits: Renders the embedded PDF pages rather than Illustrator's native editable objects; %d in the output name is replaced with the page number.
